skills.name: Comparatives and superlatives: form and scope

note.text: Comparatives relate a quality across a comparison, as in clearer than this version. Superlatives identify an extreme within a stated group, as in the clearest of these drafts. Many short adjectives take er and est; some longer forms use more and most. Irregular patterns include good, better, best. Avoid double marking such as more clearer. A comparative claim must say or imply a sensible comparison basis.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to form a comparison and distinguish a pairwise judgement from a group maximum. Builds on: modifiers and editing. Leads to: precise descriptive writing.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern
sections.text: Comparatives relate a quality across a comparison, as in clearer than this version. Superlatives identify an extreme within a stated group, as in the clearest of these drafts. Many short adjectives take er and est; some longer forms use more and most. Irregular patterns include good, better, best. Avoid double marking such as more clearer. A comparative claim must say or imply a sensible comparison basis.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Draft B is clearer than Draft A for the stated audience. Among the displayed drafts, B is the clearest. These judgements concern a criterion and group; they do not prove B is the best text ever written. More useful is the selected longer-adjective model, while better is the irregular comparison of good.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Identify the quality, comparison set and required degree. Choose the appropriate form, then check than for the comparative model and a clear group for the superlative. Do not combine both methods of marking the same degree.

cards.idea: Read the whole example before identifying its function.
example: Clearer than Draft A compares clarity.
The clearest of the displayed drafts refers to that group.
Good has the comparative better in the model.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: More clearer is the taught edited form. Correction: Do not double-mark this comparative.
The clearest here proves the best in every possible context. Correction: The claim is limited to its group and criterion.
Gooder is the model comparative of good. Correction: Use the established irregular form.
A comparison never needs a relevant criterion. Correction: The criterion and reference matter to meaning.
